headline: S. 4003 did not pass; it would have directed the Justice Department to create law enforcement training on de-escalation and crisis response and to fund state training grants.
what_it_does: The measure would have required the Department of Justice to develop scenario-based training materials, or identify existing ones, on alternatives to force, de-escalation tactics, and safely responding to people in mental, behavioral health, or suicidal crises. It would also have directed the Department to give grants to states to cover the costs of providing this training. The House voted it down on November 29, 2022, so none of these changes were made.

who_it_affects.how: They would have been eligible for training on de-escalation and on responding to people in mental health or suicidal crises.
They could have received the same training funded through the state grants.
They would have been able to apply for federal grants to pay for providing this training.

who_it_affects.group: People experiencing mental, behavioral health, or suicidal crises
who_it_affects.how: They would have been affected indirectly if officers and responders received more training on safe crisis response.
